title: Welded Asteroids
description: The closed-loop stigmergic field itself, living on the quotient surfaces of the topology game: physarum agents, trail and agent-deposited momentum all obey the surface's gluing rule. Six tour levels bind surface + parameter presets + a beta_1 target; 18 declared sliders drive the physarum; the asteroids game survives as a hidden Easter egg (X when beta_1 >= 42). v2.0.1: seam crossings now transform position AND heading together (topo-asteroids flipP protocol — fixes agents stranding at the Klein/projective seams); sim square letterboxed to true 1:1 (fixes stretched height map). v2.1.0: the real fix for the Klein seam-wall — three compounding defects. (1) foldRead/momRead/uvOf mirrored the WRONG axis (topo.y.flip='x' names the axis that mirrors; the code mirrored the other one), so agent sensing disagreed with deposits. (2) Diffusion sampled neighbors with plain torus wrap; on a mirrored identification the flux at the seam never cancels and mass was slowly pumped into the two seam rows — the minutes-scale accumulator. Now neighbor sampling honors the gluing rule (mirrored cell across a mirrored seam) for trail AND momentum, with the vector's mirrored component sign-flipping. (3) Sense samples crossing a mirrored seam have swapped left/right meaning relative to the agent's square frame; the turn rule now swaps L/R when the front and a flank read different fold images — near-seam agents no longer turn back into the seam. Also fixed: wrapPos wrap-count for negative coordinates (floor division) and double-flip when a y-fold pushed x out of range. Verified: 150s Klein soak — no seam wall, no edge pinning; torus/projective/Mobius 45s soaks all stable. v2.2.0: the height map projects the topology — 3D vertices displace along their base normal by the folded trail height (ridges = built loops, valleys = evaporated field), texture texels fold so the parametrization shows the true pullback at every seam, contour lines and agent points ride the same displaced surface, and a '3D relief' slider (0..1) controls the amplitude. Lit MeshStandardMaterial with key/rim lights so relief reads as form. v2.3.0: color separation + seam-continuous contours. Chemical field stays green; contour overlays recolored to the violet family; agents drawn as cyan-white dots (2D overlay + 3D points) so they read against the chemical; wireframe seam guides dimmed violet. Contour segments touching a canvas edge are redrawn shifted by the wrap so closed loops read continuously across the weld instead of chopping off. v2.3.1: operator-reported 3D misalignment (left planes not lining up) — root cause: the v2.2.0 texture/relief path folded the uv a second time (guessing the parametrization needed the sim's mirror), but the surface parametrization already IS the folded immersion; the extra fold split the texture along a line the geometry never folds. foldUv is now the identity — the gluing lives in the parametrization and the sim-side foldRead, exactly once each. v2.3.2: Codex co-review (gpt-6-astra, read-only) confirmed the operator's residual 3D misalignment was a VERTICAL TEXTURE FLIP — three.js CanvasTexture defaults flipY=true, so texture rows ran opposite to the height sampling rows. Fixed with flipY=false. Two follow-on defects from the same review: entities (contours, agent points) now ride the ACTUAL displaced mesh via barycentric interpolation instead of the analytic surface (they floated/sank between mesh vertices), and relief 0 now restores base positions instead of freezing the last displacement. v2.3.3: hardened the overlay against a devicePixelRatio desync — the canvas is sized and transformed with the DPR live at fit time, but the draw paths re-read devicePixelRatio, and a window dragged to a display of different pixel density changes it without firing resize. Scale is now committed once per fit (ovSX/ovSY), a matchMedia (resolution: Ndppx) listener refits on density change, and a ResizeObserver on the sim panel covers layout changes that never resize the window. NOTE: this was a real latent defect but NOT the cause of the operator's report — see v2.3.4. v2.3.4: the actual cause of the operator-reported quarter-size overlay — drawContours computed the grid→CSS scale and then never applied it. buildContour emits paths in GRID units (0..W) because segStore is reused for the 3D push, so the strokes must carry the scale themselves; without it contours drew one grid unit per CSS pixel, filling a W-sized patch in the top-left of an s-sized box. The error is W/s, so it is invisible when the sim panel is about W wide and grows with the window — which is why it read as 'quarter size' on a wide window and looked fine on a narrow one. Strokes now run under octx.scale(sx,sy) with line widths divided back out so the authored weights hold; segStore stays in grid units for the 3D push. The test port exposes __welded.ovScale so the registration can be measured rather than eyeballed. Verified at a 1355x760 viewport: violet contour centroid (0.711, 0.518) against field centroid (0.716, 0.527) on the sim canvas — agreement to within 0.01 of the canvas, where the pre-fix overlay centroid sat at (0.336, 0.334) against a field centroid of (0.500, 0.498).

cogdoc.claim: The closed-loop stigmergic field's native domain is a quotient surface: agent writes and reads both obey the surface's gluing rule (mirrored re-entry on Klein/projective/Mobius, walls on the strip), so the simulation itself provides the levels and the beta_1 readout is measured on the surface the structures actually live on.
